title: foam publishes a new data ref to origin without being asked
body:
When a clone has a remote named `origin`, `init` in `src/cmd.rs` calls `setup_sync`, which installs `.git/hooks/pre-push`. That hook runs `foam sync --remote "$1"` before every `git push` to a remote with a URL. `sync` pushes `refs/foam/data` whether or not the remote already has it, and it installs the hook itself before it pushes. So when origin has no `refs/foam/data`, `foam init` creates the ref locally and the user's next `git push` of code publishes it to origin. A single manual `foam sync` does the same. The user never asked for either.

```text
sufr main ❯ foam init
initialized refs/foam/data with prefix sufr
installed ./.git/hooks/pre-push
origin has no refs/foam/data yet; if another clone has foam data, run `foam sync` there, then `foam sync` here
```

foam has done this since commit b85f88e, which added sync. `README.md:72` documents it.

`sync --setup` does not opt in to anything today. It runs `setup_sync` with `remote_has_data` fixed at `false`, so it never adds a refspec. Its only effect beyond a plain `sync` is a printed hint when `core.hooksPath` is set or the existing pre-push hook is not a shell script.

The requirement: foam data that `init` creates stays in the local clone until the user opts in to storing it on a remote.

## Proposal

The remote is the opt-in. foam syncs with a remote only when that remote already has `refs/foam/data`. The one command that puts the ref on a remote that lacks it is `foam sync --setup`.

| command | remote has the ref | remote lacks the ref |
|---|---|---|
| `init` | fetches it, adds the refspec, installs the hook | creates the ref locally; prints that `foam sync --setup` publishes it |
| `sync` | fetches, merges, pushes, installs the hook | fails with the same hint |
| `sync` from the hook | as above | exits 0 and prints nothing |
| `sync --setup` | as plain `sync` | pushes the ref, then adds the refspec and installs the hook |

`sync` installs the hook only once the remote has the ref, after a fetch that found it or a push that created it.

`doctor` checks the hook and the refspec only when `refs/foam/origin` exists, which means this clone has fetched from or pushed to origin. The check needs no network.

## Rejected

- A per-clone config key naming the synced remote. A second clone of a repo whose origin already has data would need the key set as well, and the remote already records the same fact.

## Cost

- The default changes, so the fix ships in a minor release.
- Clones set up by an older `init` keep their hook. The hook becomes harmless, since `sync` from the hook leaves a remote without the ref alone.
- If someone deletes the ref from a remote, every clone stops syncing with it until someone runs `foam sync --setup` again.
- `README.md:72-89`, the changelog, and the tests in `tests/cli.rs` that expect `init` or `sync` to install the hook against an empty origin all change.
